61. Six Dimensions for Picking an Analytical Data Warehouse挑选分析型数据仓库的六个维度

Gleb Mezhanskiy

格列布·梅然斯基

The data warehouse (DWH) plays a central role in the data ecosystem. It is also often the most expensive piece of data infrastructure to replace, so it's important to choose the right solution and one that can work well for at least seven years. Since analytics is used to power important business decisions, picking the wrong DWH is a sure way to create a costly bottleneck for your business.

数据仓库（DWH）在数据生态中扮演核心角色。它也常常是替换起来最贵的数据基础设施，所以选对方案、选一个至少能良好工作七年的方案很重要。由于分析被用来驱动重要业务决策，选错 DWH 必然会给业务制造一个昂贵的瓶颈。

In this chapter, I propose six dimensions for evaluating a data-warehousing solution for the following use cases:

本章提出六个维度，用于为以下用例评估数据仓库方案：

  • Ingesting and storing all analytical data
    接入并存储所有分析数据
  • Executing data transformations (the T of ELT)
    执行数据转换（ELT 中的 T）
  • Serving data to consumers (powering dashboards and ad hoc analysis)
    向消费方供数（支撑仪表盘和即席分析）

Scalability可扩展性

Businesses that choose poorly scalable data warehouses pay an enormous tax on their productivity when their DWHs cannot grow anymore: queries get backlogged, users are blocked, and the company is forced to migrate to a better-scaling DWH. However, at the point you feel the pain, it's already too late: the migrations are slow (years), painful, and almost never complete. Scalability for data warehouses means three things:

选择了可扩展性差的数据仓库的企业，当 DWH 再也长不大时，要在生产力上缴纳巨额税：查询堆积、用户被阻塞、公司被迫迁到扩展性更好的 DWH。然而当你感到痛时，已经太晚了：迁移很慢（要几年）、痛苦、而且几乎从来完不成。数据仓库的可扩展性意味着三件事：

  • You can increase storage easily, whenever needed, and at a constant (if not diminishing) unit price.
    你可以在需要时轻松增加存储，单价恒定（甚至递减）。
  • You can scale computing resources to have as many data-processing jobs as you need running concurrently without slowing one another down, and to shorten the execution time of each job.
    你可以扩展计算资源，让任意数量的数据处理作业并发运行而不互相拖慢，并缩短每个作业的执行时间。
  • You can scale storage and computing resources independently of each other, depending on where the bottleneck is.
    你可以独立扩展存储和计算资源，取决于瓶颈在哪里。
— p.144 —

Price Elasticity价格弹性

Pricing of DWHs falls into two main categories:

DWH 的定价主要分两类：

  • Resource-based (e.g., pay per node of a certain configuration)
    按资源（例如按某配置的节点付费）
  • Usage-based (e.g., pay per gigabyte of data scanned or CPU time)
    按用量（例如按扫描的数据 GB 数或 CPU 时间付费）

Given the natural variability of analytical workload volume due to working hours and ETL/ELT schedules, usage-based pricing tends to be more economical for the following reasons:

由于分析负载量会因工作时间和 ETL/ELT 调度而自然波动，按用量计费往往更经济，原因如下：

  • It aligns vendor incentives to your best interest by forcing them to increase the efficiency (speed) of their software. In contrast, vendors charging you per node are incentivized to sell you more computing resources instead of improving their efficiency.
    它把厂商的激励与你的最佳利益对齐，迫使他们提高软件的效率（速度）。相反，按节点收费的厂商，激励他们卖给你更多计算资源而不是提高效率。
  • Usage-based pricing provides a clear path to cost optimization: use less to pay less. Simple tactics such as eliminating redundant subqueries in ETL processes or adding filters to dashboards are immediately effective in reducing costs.
    按用量计费提供了一条清晰的成本优化路径：用得少就付得少。像去掉 ETL 流程中冗余子查询、给仪表盘加过滤这类简单策略，能立刻见效地降低成本。

Interoperability互操作性

Simply put, you want a DWH that's easy to get data into and out of. By picking a solution that is supported by the major collection, integration, and BI vendors, you will save yourself a lot of headaches.

简单说，你想要一个数据容易进也容易出的 DWH。选一个被主流采集、集成和 BI 厂商支持的方案，能省去很多头疼事。

Querying and Transformation Features查询与转换功能

While feature requirements depend greatly on the nature of the business, keep these two considerations in mind regarding the functionality of a DWH:

虽然功能需求很大程度上取决于业务性质，但关于 DWH 的功能性，请记住以下两点：

  • Optimize for the average user. Given that the vast majority of DWH users today are not engineers by training, prioritize their experience over power features.
    为普通用户优化。鉴于今天绝大多数 DWH 用户并非科班工程师，把他们的体验置于高级功能之上。
  • Your primary DWH does not have to tackle every specialized use case, including machine learning or geospatial and time-series analysis. If the DWH is interoperable, you can always plug in specialized software for the job.
    你的主 DWH 不必包揽每一个专业用例，包括机器学习或地理空间、时间序列分析。如果 DWH 可互操作，你随时可以为这类工作插上专业软件。
— p.145 —

Speed速度

One of the common failure scenarios in data infrastructure planning is over-optimizing for speed. At a tera/petabyte scale, data warehousing is all about trade-offs. You can't get infinite scalability and subsecond query speeds at the same time. Speed matters in two primary aspects:

数据基础设施规划中常见的失败场景之一，是过度优化速度。在 TB/PB 量级，数据仓库全是权衡。你不能同时得到无限可扩展性和亚秒查询速度。速度主要在两个方面重要：

  • During workload/query development that is done on smaller data volumes, jobs should complete fast and fail fast to avoid blocking human workflows.
    在小数据量上做负载/查询开发时，作业应快速完成、快速失败，以避免阻塞人的工作流。
  • In production, "good enough" execution time is good enough as long as it is consistent and can be maintained as the data grows (see the point about scalability).
    在生产中，只要执行时间稳定、并能随数据增长维持，“足够好”的执行时间就足够好（参见可扩展性那一点）。

A TPC-DS benchmark by Fivetran shows that most mainstream (as of 2021) engines are roughly in the same ballpark in terms of performance.

Fivetran 的 TPC-DS 基准测试显示，大多数主流（截至 2021 年）引擎在性能上大致在同一量级。

Zero Maintenance零运维

Modern data warehouses are complex distributed software that is nontrivial to deploy and run, let alone develop. If you are tempted to go with a new promising open source engine, make sure to account for full cost of ownership and carefully evaluate the use case and trade-offs. Picking a DWH solution that does not require any resources for you to manage allows you to focus on building your customer-facing product.

现代数据仓库是复杂的分布式软件，部署和运行都不简单，更别说开发。如果你心动想用一个有前景的新开源引擎，一定要把总拥有成本算进去，仔细评估用例和权衡。选一个不需要你投入资源运维的 DWH 方案，能让你专注于构建面向客户的产品。

— p.146 —

62. Small Files in a Big Data World大数据世界里的小文件

Adi Polak

阿迪·波拉克

No matter whether your data pipelines are handling real-time event-driven streams, near real-time data, or batch processing jobs, when you work with a massive amount of data made up of small files, you will face the small files nightmare.

无论你的数据管道处理的是实时事件流、近实时数据还是批处理作业，当你面对由小文件组成的海量数据时，就会遭遇小文件噩梦。

What Are Small Files, and Why Are They a Problem?什么是小文件？为什么是问题？

A small file is significantly smaller than the storage block size. Yes, even with object stores such as Amazon S3 and Azure Blob, there is minimum block size. A significantly smaller file can result in wasted space on the disk, since storage is optimized by block size.

小文件就是明显小于存储块大小的文件。是的，即使是 Amazon S3 和 Azure Blob 这样的对象存储，也有最小块大小。明显过小的文件会浪费磁盘空间，因为存储是按块大小优化的。

To understand why, let's first explore how reading and writing work. For read and write operations, there is a dedicated API call. For write requests, the storage writes three components:

要理解为什么，先看看读写是怎么工作的。读和写操作都有专门的 API 调用。写请求时，存储会写入三个组成部分：

  • The data itself
    数据本身
  • Metadata with descriptive properties for indexing and data management
    带描述性属性的元数据，用于索引和数据管理
  • A globally unique identifier for identification in a distributed system
    一个全局唯一标识符，用于在分布式系统中标识

More objects stored means extra unique identifiers and extra I/O calls for creating, writing, and closing the metadata and data files.

存储的对象越多，就意味着越多的唯一标识符、以及创建/写入/关闭元数据和数据文件的额外 I/O 调用。

To read the data stored, we use an API call to retrieve a specific object. The server checks for the object's unique identifier on the storage server-side and finds the actual address and disk to read from. A hierarchy of unique identifiers helps us navigate the exabyte object storage capabilities. The more unique identifiers (objects) there are, the longer the search will take. This will result in lower throughput due to search time and disk seeks required.

要读取存储的数据，我们用一个 API 调用来取回特定对象。服务器在存储服务端检查对象的唯一标识符，找到实际要读的地址和磁盘。唯一标识符的层次结构帮我们驾驭 EB 级的对象存储能力。唯一标识符（对象）越多，搜索越久。由于搜索时间和所需的磁盘寻道，吞吐量会下降。

— p.147 —

Furthermore, this translates into an overhead of milliseconds for each object store operation since the server translates each API into remote procedure calls (RPCs). When the server reaches its limits or takes too much time to retrieve the data, your API call for reading or writing will receive an error code such as 503 (server busy) or 500 (operation timed out). Dealing with those errors is excruciating with Amazon Athena, Azure Synapse, and Apache Spark tools since they abstract the storage calls for us.

此外，由于服务器把每个 API 翻译成远程过程调用（RPC），每次对象存储操作都有毫秒级开销。当服务器到达极限或取数据过慢时，你的读写 API 调用会收到 503（服务器忙）或 500（操作超时）这类错误码。用 Amazon Athena、Azure Synapse 和 Apache Spark 时处理这些错误非常痛苦，因为它们替我们把存储调用抽象掉了。

Why Does It Happen?为什么会发生？

Let's look at three general cases resulting in small files.

我们看导致小文件的三种一般情况。

First, during the ingestion procedure, event streams originating from Internet of Things (IoT) devices, servers, or applications are translated into kilobyte-scale JSON files. Writing them to object storage without joining/bundling and compressing multiple files together will result in many small files.

第一，在接入过程中，来自物联网（IoT）设备、服务器或应用的事件流被翻译成 KB 级 JSON 文件。如果不把多个文件合并/打包并压缩就直接写入对象存储，就会产生大量小文件。

Second, small files can result from parallelized Apache Spark jobs. With either batch- or stream-processing jobs, a new file gets written per write task; more Spark writing tasks means more files. Having too many parallel tasks for the size of the data can result in many small files. Data skew can have a similar effect: if most of the data is routed to one or a few writers, many writers are left with only small chunks of data to process and write, and each of these chunks gets written to a small file.

第二，小文件可能来自并行化的 Apache Spark 作业。无论批处理还是流处理作业，每个写任务都会写一个新文件；Spark 写任务越多，文件越多。对数据量来说并行任务过多，会导致许多小文件。数据倾斜也有类似效果：如果大部分数据被路由到一个或少数几个 writer，许多 writer 只剩小数据块要处理和写入，每个小块都被写成一个小文件。

Third, over-partitioned Hive tables can result from collecting data in tables daily or hourly. As a general approach, if a Hive partition is smaller than ~256 MB, consider reviewing the partition design and tweaking the Hive merge file configurations by using hive.merge.smallfiles.avgsize and hive.merge.size.per.task.

第三，按天或按小时把数据收集到表里，会导致 Hive 表过度分区。一般做法：如果一个 Hive 分区小于约 256 MB，就考虑重新审视分区设计，并通过 hive.merge.smallfiles.avgsize 和 hive.merge.size.per.task 调整 Hive 合并文件配置。

Detect and Mitigate检测与缓解

To solve the problem of small files, first identify the root cause. Is it the ingestion procedure, or offline batch processing? Check out your Hive partition file sizes, Spark job writers in the History Server UI, and the actual files' sizes on ingestion.

要解决小文件问题，先找出根因。是接入过程还是离线批处理？查看你的 Hive 分区文件大小、History Server UI 里的 Spark 作业 writer、以及接入时实际的文件大小。

If optimizing the ingestion procedure to generate bigger files won't solve the problem, look at the Spark repartition functionality (repartition_by_range) and coalesce functionality to assemble small files together. Spark 3.0 provides partitioning hints to suggest a specific assembling strategy to the Spark SQL engine.

如果优化接入过程以生成更大的文件还不能解决问题，就用 Spark 的 repartition（repartition_by_range）和 coalesce 功能把小文件合并起来。Spark 3.0 提供了分区提示（partitioning hints），可以向 Spark SQL 引擎建议特定的组装策略。

— p.148 —

Conclusion小结

Be aware of small files when designing data pipelines. Try to avoid them, but know you can fix them too!

设计数据管道时要警惕小文件。尽量避免它们，但也要知道你是可以修好的！

References

参考文献

  • Microsoft: "Scalability and Performance Targets for Blob Storage"
    微软：《Blob 存储的可扩展性和性能目标》
  • AWS: "Optimizing Amazon S3 Performance"
    AWS：《优化 Amazon S3 性能》
— p.149 —

63. Streaming Is Different from Batch流式不同于批式

Dean Wampler, PhD

迪恩·瓦姆普勒 博士

Many organizations have a range of sophisticated analytics using tools like Hadoop, SAS, and data warehouses. These batch processes have the disadvantage of a potentially long delay between the arrival of new data and the extraction of useful information from it, which can be a competitive disadvantage. So why not move these analytics to streaming services? Why not process new data immediately and minimize delays?

许多组织用 Hadoop、SAS、数据仓库这类工具做一系列复杂分析。这些批处理流程的缺点是：从新数据到达、到从中提取有用信息之间可能有很长延迟，这在竞争中可能是劣势。那为什么不把这些分析搬到流式服务上？为什么不立刻处理新数据、最小化延迟？

Several challenges make this transition hard. First, different tools may be required. Databases may have suboptimal read and write performance for continuous streams. Use a log-oriented system as your data backplane, like Apache Kafka or Apache Pulsar, to connect streaming services, sources, and sinks.

几个挑战让这种迁移很难。首先，可能需要不同的工具。数据库对连续流的读写性能可能不够理想。用面向日志的系统作为数据背板，比如 Apache Kafka 或 Apache Pulsar，把流式服务、源和汇连起来。

Familiar analysis concepts also require rethinking. For example, what does a SQL GROUP BY query mean in a streaming context, when data keeps coming and will never stop? While SQL might seem to be a poor fit for streaming, it has emerged as a popular tool for streaming logic once you add windowing, for example over event time. A GROUP BY over windows makes sense, because the window is finite. It also enables large batch jobs to be decomposed into the small, fast increments necessary for streaming.

熟悉的分析概念也需要重新思考。例如，当数据源源不断、永不停止时，SQL 的 GROUP BY 在流式语境下意味着什么？虽然 SQL 看起来不太适合流式，但一旦加上窗口（例如基于事件时间），它就成了流式逻辑的流行工具。对窗口做 GROUP BY 是合理的，因为窗口是有限的。它还让大型批作业可以分解成流式所需的小而快的增量。

Now you're ready to deploy, but streaming services are harder to keep healthy compared to batch jobs. For comparison, when you run a batch job to analyze everything that happened yesterday, it might run for a few hours. If it fails, you'll fix it and rerun it before the next day's batch job needs to run. During its run, it might encounter hardware and network outages, or it might see data spikes, but the chances are low. In contrast, a streaming service might run for weeks or months. It is much more likely to encounter significant traffic growth and spikes, and to suffer hardware or network outages. Ensuring reliable, scalable operation is both harder and more important, as you now expect this service to always be available, because new data never stops arriving.

现在你准备好部署了，但流式服务比批作业更难保持健康。对比一下：你跑一个批作业分析昨天发生的所有事，它可能跑几小时。如果失败，你修好它、在第二天批作业运行前重跑就行。在运行期间，它可能遇到硬件和网络故障，也可能遇到数据尖峰，但概率低。相反，一个流式服务可能跑几周或几个月。它遇到显著流量增长和尖峰、遭遇硬件或网络故障的可能性要大得多。确保可靠、可扩展的运行既更难也更重要，因为你现在期望这个服务永远可用，新数据永远不会停。

— p.150 —

The solution is to adopt the tools pioneered by the microservices community to keep long-running systems healthy, more resilient against failures, and easier to scale dynamically. In fact, now that we're processing data in small increments, many streaming services should be implemented as microservices using stream-oriented libraries like Akka Streams and Kafka Streams, rather than always reaching for the "big" streaming tools like Apache Spark and Apache Flink.

解决方案是采用微服务社区率先推出的工具，让长时间运行的系统保持健康、更能抗故障、更容易动态扩展。事实上，既然我们在以小增量处理数据，许多流式服务应该用面向流的库（如 Akka Streams 和 Kafka Streams）作为微服务实现，而不是总是伸手去拿 Apache Spark 和 Apache Flink 这类“大”流式工具。

To summarize:

总结一下：

  • Understand the volume per unit time of your data streams.
    理解你的数据流单位时间数据量。
  • Understand your latency budget.
    理解你的延迟预算。
  • Use Apache Kafka, Apache Pulsar, or similar as your data backplane.
    用 Apache Kafka、Apache Pulsar 或类似系统作为数据背板。
  • Use Apache Spark or Apache Flink when you have either large volumes or complex analytics (e.g., SQL), or both.
    当数据量大、或分析复杂（例如 SQL）、或两者兼有时，用 Apache Spark 或 Apache Flink。
  • Use microservices with stream-processing libraries like Akka Streams or Kafka Streams for lower-latency requirements and lower-volume situations.
    对于低延迟要求和较低数据量的情况，用 Akka Streams 或 Kafka Streams 这类流处理库的微服务。
— p.151 —

64. Tardy Data迟到的数据

Ariel Shaqed

阿里尔·沙克德

When collecting time-based data, some data is born late, some achieves lateness, and some has lateness thrust upon it. That makes processing the "latest" data challenging. For instance:

在收集基于时间的数据时，有些数据生下来就晚，有些是后来迟到的，有些是被强加了迟到。这让处理“最新”数据变得有挑战。例如：

  • Trace data is usually indexed by start time. Data for an ongoing interval is born late and cannot be generated yet.
    追踪数据通常按开始时间索引。一个正在进行中的区间的数据，生下来就晚，还无法生成。
  • Collection systems can work slower in the presence of failures or bursts, achieving lateness of generated data.
    采集系统在故障或突发流量时会变慢，导致生成的数据迟到。
  • Distributed collection systems can delay some data, thrusting lateness upon it.
    分布式采集系统可能延迟某些数据，把迟到强加给它。

Lateness occurs at all levels of a collection pipeline. Most collection pipelines are distributed, and late data arrives significantly out of order. Lateness is unavoidable; handling it robustly is essential.

迟到发生在采集管道的各个层级。大多数采集管道是分布式的，迟到数据到达时严重乱序。迟到不可避免；稳健地处理它至关重要。

At the same time, providing repeatable queries is desirable for some purposes, and adding late data can directly clash with it. For instance, aggregation must take late data into account.

同时，对某些用途来说，提供可重复查询是值得追求的，而加入迟到数据会与之直接冲突。例如，聚合必须把迟到数据考虑进去。

Common strategies align by the way they store and query late data. Which to choose depends as much on business logic as it does on technical advantages.

常见策略按其存储和查询迟到数据的方式分类。选哪个，既取决于技术优势，也同样取决于业务逻辑。

Conceptually, the simplest strategy is to update existing data with late data. Each item of data, no matter how late, is inserted according to its timestamp. This can be done in a straightforward manner with many databases. It can be performed with simple data storage. But any scaling is hard; for example, new data files or partitions need to be generated for late data. There is no repeatability (very late data might have arrived between repetitions of the same query), and any stored aggregations must be augmented, reprocessed, or dropped. This method is mostly suited for smaller scales.

从概念上讲，最简单的策略是用迟到数据更新已有数据。每条数据无论多晚，都按其时间戳插入。许多数据库都能直接这么做。用简单数据存储就能实现。但任何扩展都很难；例如，需要为迟到数据生成新的数据文件或分区。没有可重复性（极晚的数据可能在同一查询的两次执行之间到达），任何已存储的聚合都必须增补、重处理或丢弃。这种方法主要适用于较小规模。

Bitemporal modeling lets us add repeatability. If we add a second serialized storage arrival time field to all data, every query for analytics or aggregation can filter times by timestamp and then by a storage arrival time that is known (by serialization) to be in the past. Aggregates include the upper storage arrival time in their metadata, allowing queries to use them by filtering for the data that arrived later.

双时间建模让我们可以加上可重复性。如果我们给所有数据加第二个序列化的存储到达时间字段，每个分析或聚合查询都可以先按时间戳过滤、再按一个已知（通过序列化）在过去的存储到达时间过滤。聚合在元数据中包含上层存储到达时间，让查询可以通过过滤“更晚到达”的数据来使用它们。

— p.152 —

Another option is to ignore late data. Set a fixed deadline interval. Any data that arrives before the deadline is released for access and any data arriving later than the deadline is dropped (preferably with some observability). This is a simple option to understand, implement, and scale. But for repeatability, it delays all data by the deadline interval, even when all data arrives on time. So, it is most directly useful if there is a relevant deadline value.

另一个选项是忽略迟到数据。设定一个固定的截止区间。在截止时间之前到达的数据被释放以供访问，晚于截止时间到达的数据被丢弃（最好带一些可观测性）。这是一个容易理解、实现和扩展的选项。但为了可重复性，它会把所有数据延迟一个截止区间，即使所有数据都准时到达。因此，当存在相关的截止值时，它最直接有用。

Combine ignoring late data with an effective arrival time by layering multiple instances of this strategy. Set a sequence of deadline intervals. Data goes into the first layer not beyond its deadline, giving a quantized arrival time. Equivalently, data collection keeps a sequence of buckets with increasing deadlines. When a deadline expires, its bucket is sealed and a new one is opened with the same deadline. Queries are for a particular time and use only buckets that were sealed at that time; the time is part of the query, ensuring repeatability.

把“忽略迟到数据”与一个有效到达时间结合起来，方法是把这种策略叠多层。设定一系列截止区间。数据进入第一层不超过其截止时间，得到一个量化的到达时间。等价地说，数据采集维护一串截止时间递增的桶。当一个截止时间到期，它的桶被封上，开一个新桶、同样的截止时间。查询针对某个特定时间，只使用在该时间已被封上的桶；时间是查询的一部分，从而保证可重复性。

— p.153 —

65. Tech Should Take a Back Seat for Data Project Success技术应在数据项目成功中退居二线

Andrew Stevenson (Cofounder and CTO, Lenses.io)

安德鲁·史蒂文森（Lenses.io 联合创始人兼 CTO）

Data has always been a constant in my career. From my early days as a C++ developer through my switch to data engineering, my experience managing increasing velocities and volumes of data for use cases such as high-frequency trading has forced me to lean on cutting-edge open source technologies.

数据一直是我职业生涯中的常数。从早期做 C++ 开发者、到转向数据工程，我为高频交易等用例管理越来越高速、越来越大量的数据，这迫使我依赖前沿开源技术。

I was one of the fortunate ones. I worked with an elite set of handsomely paid developers, at the peak of the big data revolution. Cutting-edge as we were, managing the technology wasn't our biggest challenge. Our top challenge was understanding the business context and what to do with the technology. As a dev, I shouldn't be expected to configure complex infrastructure, build and operate pipelines, and also be an expert in credit market risk.

我是幸运者之一。在大数据革命的顶峰，我和一队高薪精英开发者一起工作。尽管我们很前沿，管理技术并不是我们最大的挑战。我们最大的挑战是理解业务上下文、以及用技术做什么。作为开发者，不能指望我既配置复杂基础设施、搭建和运维管道，又是信贷市场风险专家。

Time and again, I witnessed business analysts sidelined in favor of data engineers who spent all day battling open source technologies with little or no familiarity with the context of the data or the intended outcome. The technology-first focus often led to Resume++, where technologists were empowered and enamored with technology rather than focusing on business objectives.

我一次又一次看到业务分析师被边缘化，取而代之的是数据工程师——他们整天和开源技术搏斗，对数据的上下文或预期结果几乎不了解。这种技术优先的关注常常导致“简历++”：技术人被赋能、迷恋技术，而不是聚焦业务目标。

The result was slow progress, project failures, and budget overruns. This especially hurt businesses during the 2008 crash, and we're seeing that impact again starting in 2020 with COVID-19.

结果是缓慢的进展、项目失败和预算超支。这在 2008 年金融危机期间尤其伤害企业，而从 2020 年新冠疫情开始，我们又看到了这种影响。

The greatest success and innovation I've witnessed occurs when end users (business users, data analysts, data scientists) are given the correct tooling and the access to explore, process, and operate data themselves.

我所见过的最大成功和创新，发生在终端用户（业务用户、数据分析师、数据科学家）被给予正确工具、以及自己探索、处理和操作数据的访问权时。

Modern data platforms are distributed, generally open source, and their tooling, if any, isn't enterprise-ready. Therefore, organizations must turn to hard-to-find and highly skilled engineers. Unfortunately, these engineers have a limited understanding of the data and the business context.

现代数据平台是分布式的、通常是开源的，它们的工具（如果有的话）还没到企业级。因此组织必须求助于难招、高技能的工程师。不幸的是，这些工程师对数据和业务上下文的理解有限。

— p.154 —

Some organizations with "elite" R&D teams develop self-service tools at a huge expense. For those without the elite resources, these technologies are much less accessible. This exacerbates the divide between the web-scale companies (such as Google, Spotify, Uber, and Amazon) and the rest of the industry.

一些拥有“精英”研发团队的组织花巨资开发自助工具。对那些没有精英资源的组织来说，这些技术遥不可及。这加剧了 Web 规模公司（如 Google、Spotify、Uber、Amazon）与行业其他公司之间的鸿沟。

Technology should be an enabler to deliver data products. To achieve this, best-of-breed technologies should be available in a data mesh type of architecture with a decoupled self-service and governance layer. This allows end users to apply DataOps practices to operate data and applications without infrastructure knowledge. Workloads should include data cataloging, role-based access control (RBAC) options, data masking, and the ability to create virtual workspaces that allow teams to explore, process, and move data through low-code applications.

技术应该是交付数据产品的使能器。要实现这一点，最佳技术应在数据网格类架构中可用，并配一个解耦的自助和治理层。这让终端用户可以应用 DataOps 实践来操作数据和应用，而无需基础设施知识。工作负载应包括数据编目、基于角色的访问控制（RBAC）选项、数据掩码，以及创建虚拟工作区的能力——让团队通过低代码应用来探索、处理和移动数据。

Cloud providers have created "technology intensity" by offering managed solutions for Apache Kafka such as Amazon MSK, Azure HDInsight, and Kubernetes. So, the role of data engineers should shift away from building pipelines and operating data infrastructure, to focus on delivering self-service tooling that allows end users to operate data themselves and build "data intensity."

云厂商通过提供 Apache Kafka 的托管方案——如 Amazon MSK、Azure HDInsight 和 Kubernetes——创造了“技术强度”。因此，数据工程师的角色应从搭建管道和运维数据基础设施，转向交付自助工具，让终端用户自己操作数据、构建“数据强度”。

— p.155 —

66. Ten Must-Ask Questions for Data-Engineering Projects数据工程项目必问的十个问题

Haidar Hadi

海达尔·哈迪

Think of this as a checklist of the questions that you need to ask before giving an estimate of when you will deliver or when you will start design. And you definitely need to ask these questions before coding.

把这当作一份问题清单：在你给出交付时间或开始设计的估算之前，你需要问这些问题。而且你一定要在写代码之前问这些问题。

Question 1: What Are the Touch Points? Identify all the data sources that the data pipeline will be leveraging. Also identify all the output locations/systems that will be using the data product your pipeline produces, along with systems that contain configurations, lookups, etc.

问题 1：接触点有哪些？识别数据管道将利用的所有数据源。还要识别将使用你管道所产出数据产品的所有输出位置/系统，以及包含配置、查找表等的系统。

Question 2: What Are the Granularities? For a given data source, do not assume (based on the sample dataset) the granularity it represents. A given dataset may represent a transaction, a company, a combination of both, or an aggregation based on a certain level of granularity. Ask about the level of granularity on both the input data source and the output data source. For example, ask the following:

问题 2：粒度是什么？对一个给定数据源，不要（基于样本数据集）假设它表示的粒度。一个给定数据集可能表示一笔交易、一家公司、两者结合，或基于某一粒度水平的聚合。对输入数据源和输出数据源都要问粒度水平。例如问：

  • Does the data object represent data on the transaction level; the transaction level rolled up to monthly, quarterly, or annually; or in a moving window?
    这个数据对象是交易级数据？还是按交易级汇总到月、季、年？还是移动窗口？
  • Does the data object represent data on the customer level (either an individual or a group of customers)?
    这个数据对象是客户级数据（个人或客户群）？
— p.156 —

Question 3: What Are the Input and Output Schemas? Ask for the schemas for the input data sources and the output data sources before you start coding. Provide a sample output based on the input schema and the requirements you are given.

问题 3：输入和输出 schema 是什么？在开始写代码之前，要输入数据源和输出数据源的 schema。基于输入 schema 和给你的需求，提供一个输出样本。

Question 4: What Is the Algorithm? Most of the dataset produced by the data-engineering team will be fed into an algorithm that will produce a calculation or prediction. Make sure you understand the input for such an algorithm and compare it with the output dataset that you are supposed to produce. At the end of the day, the output produced by your data pipeline must have all the input elements to the algorithm at all stages.

问题 4：算法是什么？数据工程团队产出的大多数数据集，会喂给一个算法来产生计算或预测。务必理解这种算法的输入，并与你应产出的输出数据集对比。归根结底，你的数据管道产出的输出，在所有阶段都必须包含算法所需的全部输入元素。

Question 5: Do You Need Backfill Data? Many algorithms use heuristics to build better predictions. However, during development, data scientists may focus on a smaller dataset, but still expect the full history backfill during production. Such requirements have an impact on development efforts, delivery date, resources, and cost.

问题 5：需要回填数据吗？许多算法用启发式来构建更好的预测。然而在开发期间，数据科学家可能聚焦于较小数据集，但在生产中仍期望全历史回填。这种需求会影响开发工作量、交付日期、资源和成本。

Question 6: When Is the Project Due Date? In many cases, the project may have dependencies on other projects. Clarify the due date in reference to other dependencies.

问题 6：项目截止日期是什么时候？很多情况下，项目可能依赖其他项目。参照其他依赖项把截止日期搞清楚。

Question 7: Why Was That Due Date Set? Now that you have clarified the project due date, please clarify the rationale behind it, as it may lead to more projects. Agreeing to a project due date without understanding its impact on the following project may give a false impression that you will be delivering multiple projects.

问题 7：为什么定这个截止日期？既然你已经搞清了项目截止日期，请搞清背后的理由，因为它可能引出更多项目。在不理解该截止日期对下一个项目影响的情况下答应它，可能会给人一种你能交付多个项目的错误印象。

Question 8: Which Hosting Environment? Ask for clarification on where the data pipeline will be running. Is it going to be hosted internally or on the cloud? What cloud accounts, permissions to the datasets, and resources will you be using?

问题 8：哪个托管环境？问清楚数据管道将在哪里运行。是内部托管还是云上？你会用哪些云账户、数据集权限和资源？

— p.157 —

Question 9: What Is the SLA? Are the datasets produced in real time? In batches? When are they supposed to be delivered to the customer?

问题 9：SLA 是什么？数据集是实时产出的？还是批处理？它们应该在什么时候交付给客户？

Question 10: Who Will Be Taking Over This Project? Many projects will be maintained by other people. Ask about their skill level and the kind of documentation they need to operate your data pipeline.

问题 10：谁来接手这个项目？许多项目会由别人维护。问清楚他们的技能水平、以及他们需要什么样的文档来运维你的数据管道。

— p.158 —

67. The Data Pipeline Is Not About Speed数据管道不是关于速度

Rustem Feyzkhanov

鲁斯捷姆·费兹哈诺夫

Data-processing pipelines used to be about speed. Now we live in a world of public cloud technologies, where any company can provide additional resources in a matter of seconds. This fact changes our perspective on the way data processing pipelines should be constructed.

数据处理管道过去是关于速度的。现在我们活在一个公有云技术的世界，任何公司都能在几秒钟内提供额外资源。这个事实改变了我们对数据处理管道应如何构建的看法。

In practice, we pay equally for using 10 servers for 1 minute and 1 server for 10 minutes. Because of that, the focus has shifted from optimizing execution time to optimizing scalability and parallelization. Let's imagine a perfect data-processing pipeline: 1,000 jobs get in, are processed in parallel on 1,000 nodes, and then the results are gathered. This would mean that on any scale, the speed of processing doesn't depend on the number of jobs and is always equal to that of one job.

实际上，我们用 10 台服务器跑 1 分钟和用 1 台服务器跑 10 分钟付的钱一样。因此，焦点从优化执行时间转移到了优化可扩展性和并行化。想象一个完美的数据处理管道：1000 个作业进来，在 1000 个节点上并行处理，然后收集结果。这意味着在任何规模下，处理速度都不依赖于作业数量，永远等于一个作业的速度。

And today this is possible with public cloud technologies like serverless computing that are becoming more and more popular. They provide a way to launch thousands of processing nodes in parallel. Serverless implementations like AWS Lambda, Microsoft Azure Functions, and Google Cloud Functions enable us to construct scalable data pipelines with little effort. You just need to define libraries and code, and you are good to go. Scalable orchestrators like AWS Step Functions and Azure Logic Apps allow executing hundreds or thousands of jobs in parallel. Services like AWS Batch allow you to easily start a big cluster of instances with low Spot prices, use it to process jobs at scale, and terminate the cluster.

而今天，借助越来越流行的无服务器计算等公有云技术，这是可能的。它们提供了一种并行启动数千个处理节点的方式。AWS Lambda、Microsoft Azure Functions、Google Cloud Functions 这类无服务器实现，让我们能轻松构建可扩展的数据管道。你只需定义库和代码，就能开跑。AWS Step Functions 和 Azure Logic Apps 这类可扩展编排器，允许并行执行成百上千个作业。AWS Batch 这类服务，让你可以轻松用低价 Spot 实例起一个大集群、用它大规模处理作业、然后终止集群。

In addition, more and more vendors are introducing containers as a service, meaning that after you define an entity (e.g., Docker), it will be deployed and executed in parallel and you will pay only for processing time. Scalability is becoming low-hanging fruit that allows us to decrease processing times from days to hours and from hours to minutes.

此外，越来越多厂商推出容器即服务，意味着你定义好一个实体（例如 Docker）之后，它会被并行部署和执行，你只为处理时间付费。可扩展性正在变成唾手可得的东西，让我们把处理时间从几天降到几小时、从几小时降到几分钟。

But once we achieve perfect horizontal scalability, should we focus on execution time? Yes, but for a different reason. In a world of perfect horizontal scalability, execution time doesn't influence the speed of processing the batch much, but it significantly influences the cost. Optimizing speed twice means optimizing cost twice, and that is the new motivation for optimization. This way, a decision about optimization becomes a decision about cost, which has a very clear return on investment (ROI). Even more, designing an absolutely scalable data pipeline without taking optimization of algorithms into account at all can lead to an extremely high cost for the pipeline. That is one of the disadvantages of a system that doesn't have an economy of scale. The emerging opportunity is to design data pipelines to optimize unit costs and enable scalability from the initial phases, allowing transparent communication between data engineers and other stakeholders such as project managers and data scientists.

但一旦我们实现了完美的水平扩展，我们还该关注执行时间吗？是的，但原因不同。在完美水平扩展的世界里，执行时间对批处理速度影响不大，但它显著影响成本。把速度优化一倍就意味着把成本优化一倍，这才是优化的新动机。这样一来，关于优化的决策就变成了关于成本的决策，有非常清晰的投资回报（ROI）。更进一步，设计一个绝对可扩展的数据管道、却完全不考虑算法优化，可能导致管道成本极高。这是缺乏规模经济的系统的缺点之一。新出现的机会是：设计数据管道时优化单位成本、并从初始阶段就支持可扩展性，让数据工程师与项目经理、数据科学家等其他利益相关者之间能透明沟通。

— p.159 —
— p.160 —

68. The Dos and Don'ts of Data Engineering数据工程的该做与不该做

Christopher Bergh (CEO and head chef at DataKitchen)

克里斯托弗·伯格（DataKitchen CEO 兼主厨）

Here are the things that I wish I had known when I started out in the data industry years ago.

下面是我多年前刚进入数据行业时希望自己就知道的事。

Don't Be a Hero别当英雄

Data analytics teams work long hours to compensate for the gap between performance and expectations. When a deliverable is met, the data analytics team are considered heroes. Everyone loves to get awards at the company meeting; however, heroism is a trap.

数据分析团队靠长工时来弥补表现与预期之间的差距。当一个交付物被完成时，数据分析团队被视为英雄。人人都爱在公司大会上拿奖；然而英雄主义是个陷阱。

Heroes give up work/life balance. Yesterday's heroes are quickly forgotten when there is a new crisis or deliverable to meet. The long hours eventually lead to burnout, anxiety, and even depression. Heroism is difficult to sustain over a long period of time, and it ultimately just reinforces the false belief that the resources and methodologies in place are adequate.

英雄放弃了工作/生活平衡。当新危机或新交付物出现时，昨天的英雄很快被遗忘。长工时最终导致倦怠、焦虑甚至抑郁。英雄主义很难长期维持，它最终只是强化了一个错误信念：现有的资源和方法是足够的。

Don't Rely on Hope别指望希望

When a deadline must be met, it is tempting to quickly produce a solution with minimal testing, push it out to the users, and hope it does not break. This approach has inherent risks. Eventually, a deliverable will contain errors, upsetting users and harming the hard-won credibility of the data analytics team.

当截止日期必须赶上时，人很容易快速产出一个方案、最少测试、推给用户，然后希望它别坏。这种方法有固有风险。最终，某个交付物会包含错误，惹恼用户、伤害数据分析团队来之不易的信誉。

Many data professionals will recognize this situation. You work late on Friday night to get high-priority changes completed. After a heroic effort, you get it done and go home. Saturday morning you wake up, startled. "I forgot to check X. Did I just break the analytics?" You can either rush back to work and spend the weekend testing, or let it go and hope everything is OK. In this context, hope is not a strategy on which to bank your reputation. You may get away with it a few times, until you don't.

许多数据人会认出这个场景。你周五晚上加班把高优先级变更做完。经过一番英雄式努力，你完成了、回家了。周六早上你惊醒。“我忘了检查 X。我是不是把分析搞坏了？”你要么冲回公司、花整个周末测试，要么随它去、希望一切 OK。在这种语境下，希望不是一个可以拿来赌上你声誉的策略。你可能侥幸几次，但总有一次不行。

— p.161 —

Don't Rely on Caution别靠谨慎

When the team finally buys into testing, a common mistake is to slow everything down. The project manager gives each data analytics project a longer development and testing schedule. Effectively, this is a decision to deliver higher quality but fewer features to users. Do this, and the data analytics team risks being viewed as bureaucratic and inefficient. Soon the VPs will each have their own data analyst on staff, and they'll wonder exactly what it is that you do.

当团队最终接受测试时，一个常见错误是把一切都放慢。项目经理给每个数据分析项目更长的开发和测试排期。实际上，这是一个“交付更高质量、但给用户更少功能”的决策。这么做，数据分析团队就有被视为官僚和低效的风险。很快各位 VP 都会自己配数据分析师，他们会纳闷你到底是干什么的。

Do DataOps做 DataOps

For many years, I accepted these things as just part of the job of a data professional. Then I realized that no, it doesn't have to be that way. I found that the software and manufacturing industries had been struggling with these same issues for decades. When I applied their methodologies to data engineering, I found my team could decrease the analytics cycle time and virtually eliminate errors.

多年来，我把这些事当成数据人工作的一部分。后来我意识到，不，不必这样。我发现软件和制造业几十年来一直在和同样的问题搏斗。当我把他们的方法应用到数据工程时，我发现我的团队可以缩短分析周期、几乎消除错误。

This new approach is called DataOps, and you can implement it alongside your existing toolchain:

这种新方法叫 DataOps，你可以在现有工具链旁边实施它：

  • Automate the creation of development sandboxes with data for data scientists.
    为数据科学家自动创建带数据的开发沙箱。
  • Use containers and other tools that simplify reuse.
    使用容器和其他简化复用的工具。
  • Manage parallel development and align toolchains with environments and source control.
    管理并行开发，让工具链与环境和源码控制对齐。
  • Push new analytics into operations by using DevOps continuous deployment.
    用 DevOps 持续部署把新分析推到生产。
  • Create automated impact reviews and test, test, test.
    创建自动化影响评审，测试、测试、再测试。
  • Orchestrate the code deployment and data operations pipelines, including tests.
    编排代码部署和数据操作管道，包括测试。
  • Architect for rapid change and quick recovery from outages. Design for the cycle time that you want.
    为快速变更和快速从故障恢复而架构。按你想要的周期时间来设计。

When tests validate data flowing through the pipeline and also ensure the quality of all new and updated analytics, the error rate declines until errors are basically eliminated. There's no more need for heroism because the data pipelines are much more robust. There's no need for hope because your tests prove that the data and analytics are working. Most importantly, trust is maintained because analytics work as expected, and when they don't, the data team is activated with automated alerts. You'll know before the users, and they'll thank you when you call to give them a heads-up.

当测试既校验流经管道的数据、又确保所有新分析和更新分析的质量时，错误率会下降，直到错误基本被消除。不再需要英雄主义，因为数据管道健壮得多。不再需要希望，因为你的测试证明数据和分析在正常工作。最重要的是，信任得以维持，因为分析按预期工作；当不工作时，数据团队会被自动告警激活。你会比用户更早知道，当你打电话提醒他们时，他们会感谢你。

The bottom line here is that methodology and tools matter more than heroism. Automate everything that can be automated, and focus your attention on the creativity that requires a human touch.

底线是：方法论和工具比英雄主义更重要。把能自动化的一切自动化，把注意力放在需要人的创造力上。

— p.162 —
— p.163 —

69. The End of ETL as We Know It我们所知的 ETL 的终结

Paul Singman

保罗·辛曼

If you're as sick of this three-letter term as I am, you'll be happy to know there is another way.

如果你和我一样对这个三字母词厌烦，你会高兴地知道还有另一种方式。

If you work in data in 2021, the acronym ETL is everywhere. Ask certain people what they do, and their whole response will be "ETL." On LinkedIn, thousands of people have the title "ETL developer." It can be a noun, a verb, an adjective, and even a preposition. (Yes, a mouse can ETL a house.)

如果你 2021 年在数据行业工作，ETL 这个缩写无处不在。问某些人做什么，他们的全部回答就是“ETL”。在 LinkedIn 上，成千上万人的头衔是“ETL 开发者”。它可以是名词、动词、形容词，甚至介词。（是的，老鼠可以 ETL 一座房子。）

Standing for extract, transform, load, ETL refers to the general process of taking batches of data out of one database or application and loading them into another. Data teams are the masters of ETL, as they often have to stick their grubby fingers into the tools and databases of other teams—the software engineers, marketers, and operations folk—to prep a company's data for deeper, custom analyses.

ETL 代表抽取、转换、加载，指把一批批数据从一个数据库或应用取出、加载到另一个的一般过程。数据团队是 ETL 的大师，因为他们常常要把脏手指伸进其他团队的工具和数据库——软件工程师、市场、运营——来为公司更深、更定制的分析准备数据。

The good news is that with a bit of foresight, data teams can remove most of the ETL onus from their plate entirely. How is this possible?

好消息是，只要有点远见，数据团队可以把大部分 ETL 负担完全从自己肩上拿掉。这怎么可能？

Replacing ETL with Intentional Data Transfer用有意数据传输取代 ETL

The path forward is with intentional transfer of data (ITD). The need for ETL arises because no one builds their user database or content management system (CMS) with downstream analytics in mind. Instead of making the data team select * from purchases_table where event_date > now() - 1hr every hour, you can add logic in the application code that first processes events and emits them in a pub/sub model (see the following figure). With no wasted effort, the data team can set up a subscriber process to receive these events and process them in real time (or store them durably in S3 for later use). All it takes is one brave soul on the data team to muster the confidence to ask this of the core engineering squad.

前进的道路是有意数据传输（ITD）。需要 ETL，是因为没人在建用户数据库或内容管理系统（CMS）时把下游分析考虑在内。与其让数据团队每小时跑一次 select * from purchases_table where event_date > now() - 1hr，不如在应用代码里加逻辑：先处理事件、再以发布/订阅模型发出来（见下图）。不费什么事，数据团队就可以建一个订阅进程来接收这些事件并实时处理（或持久化存到 S3 供以后使用）。数据团队只需要一个勇敢的人，鼓起信心向核心工程组提出这个要求。

— p.164 —

Ten years ago, data teams were beginning to establish their capabilities and needs, and such an ask might have been met with a healthy dose of resistance. A decade later, however, that excuse no longer flies. And if you are on a data team doing solely traditional ETL on internal datasets, it's time you upped your game.

十年前，数据团队刚开始确立自己的能力和需求，这种请求可能会遇到相当大的阻力。然而十年后，那个借口不再管用。如果你在一个数据团队、只在内部数据集上做传统 ETL，是时候提升你的水平了。

There are several other benefits to IDT worth noting.

IDT 还有其他几个值得注意的好处。

Agreeing on a Data Model Contract就数据模型契约达成一致

How many times has one team changed a database table's schema, only to later learn the change broke a downstream analytics report? It is difficult to establish the cross-team communication necessary to avoid these issues when you have ETL scripts running directly against raw database tables. With IDT, when an event occurs, it will be published with certain fields always present that are previously agreed upon and documented. And everyone knows that any change to this JSON contract needs to be communicated first.

有多少次，一个团队改了数据库表的 schema，后来才知道这个变更搞坏了下游分析报表？当你让 ETL 脚本直接跑在原始数据库表上时，很难建立避免这些问题所需的跨团队沟通。用 IDT 时，一个事件发生时会被发布出来，总是带着事先约定并文档化的某些字段。而且每个人都知道，对这个 JSON 契约的任何变更需要先沟通。

Removing Data Processing Latencies消除数据处理延迟

Most frequently, ETL jobs are run once per day, overnight. But I've also worked on projects where they've run incrementally every 5 minutes. It all depends on the requirements of the data consumers.

最常见的是，ETL 作业每天跑一次、在夜间。但我也做过每 5 分钟增量跑一次的项目。这完全取决于数据消费方的需求。

There will always be some latency between an event occurring and the data team receiving it, which introduces tricky edge cases to the data application. With IDT, however, events are published immediately as they happen. Using real-time services like Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS), Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS), and AWS Lambda, they can be responded to immediately.

在事件发生和数据团队收到它之间，总会有一些延迟，这给数据应用带来棘手的边界情况。然而用 IDT，事件一发生就被立即发布。用 Amazon SNS、Amazon SQS、AWS Lambda 这类实时服务，可以立刻响应。

— p.165 —

Taking the First Steps迈出第一步

Moving from ETL to IDT isn't a transformation that will happen for all your datasets overnight. Taking one dataset to start, though, and setting up a pub/sub messaging pattern for it is extremely doable. My advice is to find a use case that will clearly benefit from real-time data processing—whether it's a feed of users' current locations or cancellation events—and then transition it from ETL to the IDT pattern.

从 ETL 转到 IDT，不会一夜之间在你所有数据集上发生。但从一个数据集开始、为它建立发布/订阅消息模式，是完全可行的。我的建议是：找一个明显能从实时数据处理受益的用例——无论是用户当前位置的 feed 还是取消事件——然后把它从 ETL 转到 IDT 模式。

— p.166 —

70. The Haiku Approach to Writing Software写软件的俳句方法

Mitch Seymour

米奇·西摩

Haiku is a traditional form of Japanese poetry that follows a specific set of rules. Haiku are designed to evoke deep emotion or understanding by using only three lines and a fixed number of syllables. For example:

俳句是日本传统诗歌形式，遵循一套特定规则。俳句只用三行和固定音节数，来唤起深刻的情感或理解。例如：

First autumn morning
the mirror I stare into
shows my father's face.
—— Murakami Kijo

（中文译：秋日初朝/我凝视的镜中/现出父亲的脸。——村上鬼城）

（中文译：秋日初朝/我凝视的镜中/现出父亲的脸。——村上鬼城）

As my experience as a software engineer grows, I have found myself writing better software by approaching it as I would a haiku. Here are some of the lessons I've learned along the way.

随着我作为软件工程师的经验增长，我发现自己用对待俳句的方式写软件，能写出更好的软件。下面是我一路学到的一些教训。

Understand the Constraints Up Front事先理解约束

When we build software, we must often operate within a narrow set of constraints. The constraints may include the business requirements, the technologies at our disposal, the skill set or bandwidth of the team, and the time we're given for actually creating the software.

当我们构建软件时，常常必须在一组狭窄的约束内运作。约束可能包括业务需求、我们能用上的技术、团队的技能或带宽、以及我们实际被给予的时间。

Whether you're writing a haiku or software, if you ignore or don't understand the constraints of the project, you will have trouble producing what you set out to create. Instead of ignoring the constraints, aim to create something powerful or beautiful within them.

无论你在写俳句还是软件，如果你忽略或不理解项目的约束，你就难以产出你打算创作的东西。与其忽视约束，不如在约束之内创造出强大或优美的东西。

Start Strong Since Early Decisions Can Impact the Final Product强势开局，因为早期决策会影响最终产品

There's a lot of freedom in the initial stages of a project. Many engineers approach a new project in the way a painter might approach a blank canvas. They lay down some initial, wild brush strokes in the codebase with the intent to return later and add more structure or detail. This painterly approach doesn't always translate well, as the initial brush strokes often don't get layered upon at all, but are instead annotated with TODO-style comments and become permanent fixtures in the codebase.

项目初期有很多自由。许多工程师像画家面对空白画布那样面对新项目。他们在代码库里落下一些狂野的初始笔触，打算以后再回来加结构和细节。这种画家式做法并不总是奏效：初始笔触往往根本不会被继续加层，而是被 TODO 风格的注释标注，成为代码库中的永久固定装置。

— p.167 —

The haiku approach is to be careful and intentional with early decisions, so that they become a strong foundation for everything that comes after. In other words, don't write the equivalent of the following haiku in your software:

俳句方法是：对早期决策要谨慎、有意，让它们成为后续一切的坚实基础。换句话说，别在你的软件里写出下面这种俳句：

Something something  // TODO
the mirror I stare into
shows my father's face.

（中文译：某事某事 // TODO/我凝视的镜中/现出父亲的脸。）

（中文译：某事某事 // TODO/我凝视的镜中/现出父亲的脸。）

Keep It as Simple as Possible尽可能保持简单

Unnecessary complexity can ruin a project. A haiku represents a body of work with all of the fat trimmed. Your codebase should be approached with the same care, as complexity threatens the long-term maintainability of your project and makes it easy for bugs to hide.

不必要的复杂度能毁掉一个项目。俳句代表一部剔除了所有肥肉的作品。你的代码库也应以同样的态度对待，因为复杂度威胁项目的长期可维护性、让 bug 容易藏身。

Simplicity is not always easy to achieve. In fact, it is often easier to write too much code than to find simpler, more efficient implementations. For the reasons I've stated, it's worth the extra effort to trim this extra fat from your codebase and keep it as succinct and simple as possible.

简单并不总是容易达到。事实上，写太多代码往往比找到更简单、更高效的实现更容易。出于我所说的理由，把这份额外肥肉从代码库中修掉、让它尽可能简洁，是值得付出额外努力的。

Engage the Creative Side of Your Brain动用大脑的创造性一面

Writing software is an art form. It requires creativity, good decision making, and a lot of hard work. If you are uninterested in the project or the medium, it will be reflected in the final product. If you allow yourself to be challenged creatively, as a haiku writer would, you will be giving yourself an opportunity to create something impactful for your customers or business while having fun in the process.

写软件是一种艺术形式。它需要创造力、良好决策和大量努力。如果你对项目或媒介不感兴趣，这会反映在最终产品里。如果你像俳句作者那样让自己接受创造性挑战，你就给自己一个机会：在过程中获得乐趣的同时，为客户或业务创造有影响力的东西。

— p.168 —
